newsitem.title: UK: Moody's cuts C&W, ups Videotron, Bell Cablemedia.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts C&W, ups Videotron, Bell Cablemedia.

text.p: Rating agency Moody's said on Tuesday said on Tuesday it had downgraded the debt ratings of Cable & Wireless Plc (C&W) and its guaranteed subsidiaries.
At the same time Moody's said it had upgraded the ratings of Videotron Holdings Plc and Bell Cablemedia PLC.

"These rating actions --which complete a review launched in October 1996-- are in response to the recent formation of Cable & Wireless Communications (C&WC), a UK telecommunications company 52.6% owned by C&W." Moody's said in a statement.

"The new entity was created through the merger of C&W's subsidiary Mercury Communications Limited with three cable companies--Bell Cablemedia, Videotron Holdings, NYNEX CableComms Group Inc and NYNEX CableComms Group PLC."
The ratings that have been downgraded are;

Cable & Wireless Plc - $400 million 6.5 percent Eurobond fur 2003 and 200 million stg 8.75 percent Eurobond due 2012 have been cut to A3 from A2, and the short-term rating for commercial paper to Prime 2 from Prime 1.

Cable & Wireless International Finance BV (guaranteed by C&W) - 200 million stg 8.625 pct bonds due 2019, the 50 million stg 10.375 pct Eurobonds due 2002 and the 150 million stg million 10.375 pct Eurobonds due 2002 to A3 from A2.
Cable & Wireless International NA Inc (guaranteed by C&W) - short-term rating for commercial paper to Prime 2 from Prime 1.
Videotron Holdings Plc - $343 million (face-value) 11.125 percent senior discount notes due 2004 and the $256 (face-value) 11 percent senior step-up notes due 2005 to Baa3 from B3.
Bell Cablemedia Plc - $490 million (face-value) 11.95 percent senior discount notes due 2004 and $489 million (face-value) 11.875 percent senior discount debentures due 2005 to Baa3 from B2.

"The downgrades of C&W's ratings reflect the company's exposure to the higher business and financial risks of the cable communications companies which have been merged into the new entity, while the upgrades of Videotron Holdings' and Bell Cablemedia's ratings reflect the benefits they will derive from being integrated into C&WC, which has stronger operating and financial characteristics than either Bell Cablemedia or Videotron Holdings," Moody's said.
"We also expect that these entities will benefit from ownership by C&W and its other shareholders."
Moody's expects that C&WC will be a robust integrated telecommunications service provider in the UK.

"Nevertheless, C&W's consolidated debt protection ratios have already deteriorated as a result of the creation and start-up of C&WC in the increasingly competitive UK telecommunications market," Moody's said.
